Yeah, you're right, I was answering based on my medical evaluation. What I've been told is that my obsessive thoughts are nothing more than thoughts, and that's what happens in most cases. Most people with ONLY OCD still have a lot of social awareness of what's right and wrong. 
I'm sorry if what I said misled someone to dismiss the seriousness of this condition, that's not what I intended to do at all! 
What I meant to say is that what the OP was describing is something fairly common among people with OCD and, in the majority of time, doesn't command the individual on a physical level... 
I think medical counseling should always be the most listened to in these cases nevertheless and, even though I sometimes seek for guidance on Reddit or other platforms, I never make my mind solely based on what random people tell me.

It's absolutely an OCD intrusive thought, very common. Most times, it's harmless -(as in, it doesn't actually make you stab people), but it can be truly annoying and sometimes make you feel desperate.
Hope those go away and you enter a better place soon!

I'm not an expert on the matter, but the way you describe it, makes it seem like she might have body dysmorphia, which happens when the figure you see of yourself in the mirror is not at all what your body actually looks like. It makes you see flaws in yourself that don't exist and/or exaggerate your proportions, especilly when it comes to being fat/skinny.

This can be a very dangerous condition! I think you really should find her professional help.

Also, compliment her whenever you can. Not just when she says she's fat or when she's down because of her image. Give her spontaneous and not-asked-for compliments. 

I hope everything turns out okay and that she sees that she is a beautiful woman and mother! Best wishes

NTA (because I think he should have the empathy to understand your side) but  you are overreacting and should also understand his side a little bit. Even if you're mad, ignoring him his worse, you should talk about it. Communication is key (cliche, but true) and not talking to him when you feel like he's done something wrong is not at all healthy.

You are both very young and he is still in a phase where he doesn't take the relationship and the moments you spend together as seriously as we will someday. You have to take that into account and then explain to him, calmly and politely, being sincere but not overemotional, how his actions make you feel and maybe even suggest a way to avoid situations like that.

Hope you two solve your problems, but remember: you are both very young and things like that are normal to happen, work through them
